report.summary: payment-service error rate jumped from about 0.2% to 21% at 11:00 UTC, one step after the v3.2.0 deploy at 10:57 UTC. v3.2.0 changed payments-table writes (idempotency_key) and upgraded the ORM 5.x to 6.x, with the schema migration run separately. Infrastructure, database and dependency health look normal, and the payment-service log backend timed out on every query, so the leading hypothesis (deploy ahead of its schema migration) is unverified. Checkout-service errors are most likely downstream of payment-service failures.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The v3.2.0 deploy (idempotency_key writes plus ORM 5.x to 6.x) fails on payments-table writes, probably because the schema migration is missing or incompatible. Failing writes return errors to checkout, and shallow health checks do not detect it.
assumptions: The migration was not applied, which has not been verified.
Health checks do not exercise writes.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: A schema or permission change on payments-db (for example from the separately run migration) makes certain writes fail, while reads and connection counts look normal.
assumptions: The migration touched the database at about 11:00 UTC; no database change event was returned.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The external payment provider rejects or times out payment calls, causing payment failures.

observed_facts.statement: payment-service error_rate was 0.15–0.26% from 10:00 to 10:55 UTC, then 21.26% at 11:00 UTC, peaking at 23.55% at 11:10 UTC and at 20.61% at 11:30 UTC.

Change C09 (deploy v3.2.0 to payment-service, status completed) was recorded at 10:57 UTC. It adds idempotency_key to payments table writes and upgrades the ORM 5.x to 6.x; the schema migration was run separately.
payment-service request_rate stayed between 57.8 and 62.3 req/s across the window, with no step change at 11:00 UTC.
payment-service cpu_pct (31.7–33.8%) and memory_pct (53–57%) stayed flat across the window.
payment-service latency_p99_ms stayed between 434 and 465 ms before and after 11:00 UTC.
payments-db connections (116–125), cpu (33.8–35.9%), query_latency_p99 (11.6–12.5 ms) and replication lag (about 0.4 s) show no change at 11:00 UTC.
The health checks at 11:28 UTC report payment-service, payments-db, payment-provider and checkout-service as healthy; the payments-db check is SELECT 1 only.
Past incident P02 (2026-02-11) describes payment-service 500 errors and SQL column errors after an ORM migration, where the deploy shipped before its schema migration was applied.
The only infra change in the window is the node pool upgrade (C08) at 02:00 UTC, roughly nine hours before the errors began.

assumptions: The schema migration for v3.2.0 was not applied, or was applied incompletely, before traffic reached the new version (not verified; the migration record was not in the change history).
The health checks are shallow and do not exercise payments-table writes or the new ORM code path.
payment-provider status page is an accurate indicator of provider health.
checkout-service errors are caused by payment-service errors, because checkout calls payment-service synchronously (edge D04).
(unverified - no valid evidence cited) Every query to payment-service logs (WARN/ERROR, a 10:55–11:30 ERROR window, and a 'column' search) timed out after 3 attempts, so no log lines were retrieved.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The most likely cause is the v3.2.0 deploy: the new idempotency_key writes or the ORM 6.x change fail against the payments schema, which would produce a fault only on write paths and explain why health checks pass.

The fault most likely originates in payment-service, not payments-db or payment-provider. Database metrics are flat and the database health check is shallow, but the database has not been shown to be fully clean.
The incident is not explained by traffic, capacity or the 02:00 node upgrade: request rate, CPU and memory are flat, and the node upgrade was about nine hours earlier.
Confidence is limited because the log backend is unavailable, so the migration/ORM error signature has not been confirmed. The margin over the runner-up is modest.

remediation.action: Roll back payment-service to the pre-v3.2.0 version (or disable the idempotency_key write path via feature flag if one exists).
remediation.rationale: The error onset coincides with the deploy at 10:57 UTC; rollback is the fastest way to stop payment failures.

remediation.action: Check whether the v3.2.0 schema migration has been applied to payments-db, and apply it if it is missing.
remediation.rationale: Past incident P02 had the same pattern: the deploy shipped before its migration.

remediation.action: Restore log access for payment-service (the log backend timed out) and confirm the exception class and SQL error text.
remediation.rationale: Without logs the root cause is unconfirmed.

remediation.action: Watch checkout-service error rates and payment-provider responses after rollback to confirm recovery.
remediation.rationale: Confirms that checkout errors are downstream and that the provider is not involved.

remediation.action: Add a deploy gate that blocks release until schema migrations are applied.
Make health checks exercise a payments-table write path and the ORM code path.
remediation.rationale: The current health checks passed during a 21% error rate.

remediation.action: Stage ORM major-version upgrades separately from feature changes, with canary coverage.
remediation.rationale: Reduces the blast radius of combined changes.

open_questions: What exception does payment-service raise after 11:00 UTC? The log backend timed out, so this is unknown.
Was the v3.2.0 schema migration applied, and when?
Does the error rate split by endpoint or operation (idempotency writes versus reads)?
Is checkout-service's 5xx error rate tracking payment-service's, and does it have its own errors?
Could the payment-provider or a TLS certificate issue explain the failures? No evidence was found for either, but the provider check is only a status page.
